answer: Anchor identity to a berth lease. An agent joins by leasing one slip in a participating marina. The harbor master checks the lease against the port registry and records it in a shared atlas of berths, so one slip means one agent. A slip costs 120 dollars a month, leases cannot be transferred, and the harbor master cancels any duplicate claim. Twice a year the marina checks that a real boat sits in the slip. Faking a thousand agents means renting a thousand slips for 120,000 dollars a month. The ocean is wide, but a haven has only so many slips, and one boat cannot dock in two places.
